name: roc-syntax-mcp

tools.name: roc_overview
tools.description: Call once before reading, writing, or reasoning about any Roc code. The whole language and its builtins: syntax, types, operator desugaring, modules, and where LLMs get Roc wrong. Call it even when you believe you know Roc: the Zig-based compiler changed the syntax.

scope.description: One corpus only. Omit for the language plus its standard library. Pass a platform name when you already know those and need the platform API.

tools.name: get_roc_syntax
tools.description: Upstream's all_syntax_test.roc: every language construct as compiling code, the only bundled complete program. ~3.5k tokens, so pass `topic` for one construct.

topic.description: One construct, answered as search_roc_syntax does. Omit for the whole file.

tools.name: list_roc_index
tools.description: What the other tools accept. `scopes`: the corpora `scope` takes, and documented packages. `topics`: the topics `search_roc_syntax` takes. `builtin_modules`: the module paths `get_builtin_module` takes. `examples`: worked programs. `langref`: the upstream reference pages and their sections.

scope.description: For kind='topics', 'builtin_modules', 'examples': one corpus only. Omit for the working set.

page.description: For kind='langref' only: list just this page's sections.

tools.name: search_roc_syntax
tools.description: Roc syntax snippet for a topic or keyword. Topics: idioms, iterators, ranges, record_fields, derived_methods, json, hashing, operators, pattern_matching, list_patterns, tag_unions, try_operator, strings, effects, loops, conditionals, tuples, records, types, numbers, opaque, nominal, functions, static_dispatch, imports, testing, compiler, app_header, dbg_crash, platforms, builder_pattern, scripting, error_design, parser_combinators, parser_csv, parser_yaml, parser_xml, parser_markdown, parser_http, random_generators. A platform's own topics are listed by list_roc_index(kind='topics').

query.description: Topic name (e.g. 'pattern_matching'), a keyword, a package name for its page (e.g. 'roc-parser'), or an example (e.g. 'basic-cli/hello').

scope.description: Search one corpus's topics only. Omit for the working set. Name a platform (basic-webserver, basic-cli) for what a host provides, such as I/O, graphics or networking, rather than the language or the builtins.

tools.name: lookup_builtin
tools.description: Look up a builtin by name (`concat`, `Str.concat`, `List.map`, `Num.U64.from_str`). Returns signature and docstring.

name.description: Method, type, or fully-qualified name, e.g. 'Str.concat', 'Try', or 'map'.

scope.description: Read a platform other than the one this app's header imports. Rarely needed.

tools.name: get_builtin_module
tools.description: Every method in a builtin module (`Str`, `List`, `U64`, `Num.Dec`, …) as a signature list. Bare `U64` resolves to `Num.U64`. detail='full' adds docstrings and examples. For one method use `lookup_builtin`.

detail.description: 'signatures' (default) lists name and type only. 'full' adds docstrings and examples, ~5x longer.

scope.description: Read a platform other than the one this app's header imports. Rarely needed.

tools.name: roc_check
tools.description: Type-check Roc source with the real compiler. Pass `code` or `path`. Requires the Roc compiler.

code.description: Roc source to check. Not with `path`.

path.description: Absolute path to a .roc file. Not with `code`.

scope.description: Wrap headerless `code` in this platform's app. Omit if it has a header.

tools.name: roc_fmt
tools.description: Format Roc source. Pass `code` or `path`, the same either/or as `roc_check`. Never writes the file. Requires the Roc compiler.

code.description: Roc source to format. Not with `path`.

path.description: Absolute path to a .roc file. Not with `code`.

tools.name: get_roc_langref
tools.description: Fetch a page of the upstream language reference, or one section of it. This is roc-lang/roc's own docs/langref, so it is the authoritative wording where it has coverage. Sections upstream left as TODO are written here and marked inline.

section.description: Section slug within the page, e.g. 'ranges'. Omit for the whole page.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Ranked free-text search across syntax topics, builtins, platform APIs, and the upstream language reference. Use when unsure where the answer lives.

scope.description: Search one corpus only. Omit for the working set. Name a platform (basic-webserver, basic-cli) for what a host provides, such as I/O, graphics or networking, rather than the language or the builtins.

tools.name: search_builtin_signatures
tools.description: Hoogle-style structural type signature search. A type variable matches anything, so `F32 -> Try(U64, err)` finds `F32 -> Try(U64, [OutOfRange])`. `->` / `=>` prefix searches by return type. `->` / `=>` suffix searches by incomplete argument list. Argument order matters.

query.description: Type expression, e.g. `List a, (a -> b) -> List b` or `-> Bool` or `Str, U64 -> Str`.

scope.description: Search one corpus only. Omit for the working set. Name a platform (basic-webserver, basic-cli) for what a host provides, such as I/O, graphics or networking, rather than the language or the builtins.

tools.name: search_project_signatures
tools.description: Like `search_builtin_signatures` but across user project files.

query.description: Type expression, e.g. `List(a), U64 -> List(a)` or `-> Bool` or `Str, U64 ->`.

root.description: Project root, absolute. The workspace by default.

instructions: Roc language reference for the Zig-based compiler in roc-lang/roc (2026 nightlies). Before reading, writing, or reasoning about any Roc code, call `roc_overview` once. It returns the whole language and its builtins as two compact pages (~3.3k tokens), usually enough to finish the task without another call. Do this even when you believe you know Roc: the syntax changed with this compiler, so recalled Roc is unreliable (`Try` replaced `Result`, `value.method()` static dispatch is the normal style, and every builtin lives in one `Builtin.roc`). For details, use `get_roc_langref` for upstream's own prose, `get_builtin_module` / `lookup_builtin` / `search_builtin_signatures` for builtin APIs, `search_roc_syntax` for a worked example of one construct, and `roc_check` / `roc_fmt` to verify what you wrote. Name the platform in `scope` when the workspace has no app header yet: a project you are starting has no app header yet, so nothing but you knows which platform its code is for. Never request `Builtin.roc` whole. It is hundreds of thousands of tokens.
